title: Developing CIRCULIFE with patients, carers and healthcare professionals to improve care for people with peripheral arterial disease or abdominal aortic aneurysm
official: A qualitative exploration and co-creation process to finalise a complex clinical intervention for peripheral arterial diseases
summary:
Background and study aims
Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) are conditions affecting the blood vessels. People with these conditions have an increased risk of serious health problems, including heart attack, stroke and limb complications. Although medicines and lifestyle changes can reduce these risks, care and support are not always consistent across the NHS. CIRCULIFE aims to develop a practical programme to improve the overall care of people living with PAD or AAA. This stage of the study will work with patients, carers and healthcare professionals to agree what the programme should include and how it should be delivered.

Who can participate?
Patients aged 18 years or older with a confirmed diagnosis of PAD or AAA, carers or family members who support people with PAD or AAA, and healthcare professionals currently involved in PAD or AAA care may participate. Participants must be able to provide informed consent and take part in at least one relevant study activity. Interpreter support may be used where required.

What does the study involve?
Participants may take part in online Delphi surveys, workshops and co-creation sessions. In Work Package 3, participants will complete up to two online survey rounds to rate and prioritise possible components of the CIRCULIFE programme. Some participants will also take part in online or face-to-face workshops to discuss the survey findings, areas of agreement and disagreement, and barriers and enablers to delivery. In Work Package 4, patients, carers and healthcare professionals will take part in co-creation workshops to refine the programme, patient-facing resources and healthcare-professional training materials. With consent, workshops may be audio-recorded, transcribed and anonymised for analysis. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants may not receive a direct personal benefit, but their views may help develop a more practical, inclusive and patient-centred programme for people with PAD or AAA. Participation involves minimal risk. Some discussions about illness or care may be sensitive or upsetting. Participants may decline to answer questions, take a break or withdraw at any time without affecting their healthcare or professional role. Study information will be handled securely, and research outputs will use anonymised information.

Where is the study run from?
The study is led by the University of Leicester and is being conducted with University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust, including Glenfield Hospital in Leicester (UK). Study activities may take place online or face to face, depending on the activity and participant preference.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
October 2026 to September 2030

Who is funding the study?
The study is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Academy through the NIHR Research Professorship Scheme (reference NIHR306191)

Who is the main contact?

interventions.name:
This is a prospective mixed-methods qualitative consensus and co-creation study. Following eligibility assessment and informed consent, patients with peripheral arterial disease or abdominal aortic aneurysm, carers and healthcare professionals will participate in one or more study activities.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults aged 18 years or older
2. Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of peripheral arterial disease or abdominal aortic aneurysm at any stage of disease, including early diagnosis, surveillance, community management and post-surgical care; or carers/family members who support such patients
3. Healthcare professionals currently involved in peripheral arterial disease or abdominal aortic aneurysm care, including professionals working in primary, secondary or tertiary care
4. Able to provide informed consent
5. Able to participate in English, with interpreter assistance where required
6. Able and willing to complete at least one relevant study activity, such as a Delphi survey, workshop or co-creation session
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients currently participating in another qualitative study that conflicts with research concerning the management of peripheral arterial disease or abdominal aortic aneurysm
2. Individuals with acute medical instability for whom participation would be inappropriate
3. Individuals unable to provide informed consent because of severe cognitive impairment or advanced illness, where the necessary arrangements for representation have not been ethically approved
4. Healthcare professionals who are not currently involved in peripheral arterial disease or abdominal aortic aneurysm care.
5. Individuals unable to participate in at least one relevant Delphi survey, workshop or co-creation activity
